bear.writtenAnchor: Steel prices and volumes mean-revert after the 2021-2022 spike. Revenue drifts down about 2% a year from the 2025 base as imports and new domestic capacity press on pricing, and the cash margin proxy stays near the weak end of the filed decade (FY2017 and FY2025 levels). The large capital programme of FY2024-FY2025 keeps depreciation rising while contributing little incremental profit, so the return on new dollars sits below the 11% discount rate and stock compensation slowly lifts the share count. This is a case where the last five years of spending bought capacity into a softer market.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: Filed single-year growth has ranged -16.4% to +81.2% and revenue fell in FY2019, FY2020, FY2023 and FY2024; a -2% constant rate is a mild version of those down-legs and sits well inside the permitted band around the filed range (H:revenue).

operatingMargin.text: No operating margin is filed (H:margin is n/a), so the margin is proxied by (operating cash flow - D&A) / revenue: that proxy was 2.1% in FY2017 and 6.2% in FY2025, the two weakest years of the decade (H:cashflow, H:capex, H:revenue). 6% holds the company near its most recent, already-soft level.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Net investment (capex less D&A) over revenue has a filed median of 3.7%; in a downturn Nucor historically cuts capex toward D&A, as in FY2017 when capex of 449m was below D&A of 636m, so 3% net is the conservative setting (H:capex).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: The 2019-25 build raised invested capital from 12,991m to 25,616m while FY2025 operating cash flow fell to 3,234m, so recent incremental capital has earned poorly; 8% after tax sits below the 11% discount rate, which the bear case is permitted to do.

shareCount.text: Stock-based compensation has run 130m-137m a year since FY2021 and weak operating cash flow of 3,234m in FY2025 leaves little room to repurchase against capex of 3,422m, so dilution accumulates modestly over the forecast. (1.03× today's diluted count)

base.writtenAnchor: Nucor grows revenue around 4% a year, between the 6.1% eight-year window CAGR and the flat-to-down pricing of the past two fiscal years, helped by the volume recovery visible in the July 2026 quarter (+23% year on year, trailing twelve months 36.1bn against 32.5bn of FY2025 revenue). The operating margin settles near the median of the FY2017-FY2025 cash proxy (operating cash flow less D&A over revenue, roughly 10%), i.e. mid-cycle rather than peak or trough. Net reinvestment runs above the 3.7% historic median as the recent mill programme is completed but below the 6.8% of FY2025, and new capital earns about the discount rate, which is what an undifferentiated-but-efficient commodity producer should earn over a cycle.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The eight-year window CAGR is 6.1% while the two most recent full years were down then up modestly; the latest quarter grew 23% year on year to a trailing twelve months of 36.1bn against FY2025 revenue of 32.5bn, so 4% is a mid-cycle rate between the recent trough and the window average (H:revenue, H:quarter).

operatingMargin.text: With no filed operating margin (H:margin n/a), the (operating cash flow - D&A) / revenue proxy over FY2017-FY2025 runs 2.1%, 7.0%, 9.6%, 9.9%, 15.1%, 22.3%, 17.8%, 9.4%, 6.2% — a median near 9.6%. 9.5% is that mid-cycle median (H:cashflow, H:capex, H:revenue).

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Net investment over revenue was 6.8% in FY2025 (capex 3422m, D&A 1226m, revenue 32494m) against a filed median of 3.7%; 4.5% assumes the current build programme normalises part-way back toward the median (H:capex, H:revenue).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: Filed ROIC is n/a (H:returns), so new-dollar returns are proxied from the cash record: the FY2024 proxy profit of 2.9bn on 23.3bn of invested capital is about 12% and FY2025 about 8%, straddling the 11% discount rate. 11% equals the base terminal return (11.0% rate + 0 moat credit), the floor allowed for the base case.

shareCount.text: No buyback or issuance source is supplied; stock-based compensation of about 133m a year (H:cashflow) is assumed to be offset by repurchases, leaving the diluted count unchanged at 1.0. (1× today's diluted count)

bull.writtenAnchor: The new sheet, plate and downstream capacity funded by the 2.2bn-3.4bn annual capex of FY2023-FY2025 ramps into firm demand. Revenue compounds about 8% a year, in line with the 23% year-on-year growth in the latest quarter persisting into mid-cycle volumes, and the margin runs near the upper half of the filed cash-flow record (FY2021 and FY2023 proxies of 15-18%) without reaching the 2022 peak. New investment earns around 13%, above the 12.5% bull terminal hurdle, so growth adds value; the share count is held flat.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The quarter ended 2026-07-04 grew 23% year on year and lifted trailing twelve month revenue to 36.1bn versus FY2025's 32.5bn; sustaining part of that recovery as the FY2023-FY2025 capacity ramps gives 8%, above the 6.1% window CAGR but far inside the filed single-year range (H:quarter, H:revenue).

operatingMargin.text: The (operating cash flow - D&A) / revenue proxy reached 15.1% in FY2021, 22.3% in FY2022 and 17.8% in FY2023, so 14% is the upper half of the filed cash record without assuming a repeat of the 2022 peak (H:cashflow, H:capex, H:revenue; H:margin is n/a).

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Growth is funded: capex ran 3173m and 3422m against D&A of 1094m and 1226m in FY2024-FY2025, i.e. net investment of 6.8% of revenue; 5.5% keeps spending near that elevated level while a larger revenue base absorbs it (H:capex, H:revenue).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: In the strong years the cash-profit proxy on invested capital was high (FY2023: about 6.2bn on 20.8bn), so newly built mills earning 13% is consistent with the filed record; it clears the bull terminal return of 12.5% (11.0% rate + 0 moat + 1.5 bull credit) (H:returns, H:cashflow, H:capex).

shareCount.text: No share repurchase or issuance disclosure is supplied; with stock compensation of about 133m a year assumed offset by buybacks out of stronger operating cash flow, the count is held flat at 1.0 rather than shrunk on an uncited assumption (H:cashflow). (1× today's diluted count)

moatAnchor.text: The candidate mechanism is a cost advantage from scrap-based electric-arc minimills, but no moat credit can be granted: H:returns reports NOPAT and ROIC as n/a for every filed year, so no filed return supports a perpetual return above the 11.0% discount rate, and H:margin is likewise n/a. The cash-based proxy that can be built from H:cashflow and H:capex swings from about 2% to 22% of revenue across FY2017-FY2025, which is the signature of a price-taking commodity producer rather than durable pricing power. Terminal returns are therefore 11.0% (bear and base) and 12.5% (bull).

constantsAnchor.text: No company tax-rate disclosure is supplied, so the general US federal statutory rate of 21.0% is used (STATUTORY), the same rate applied in the H:returns NOPAT definition. H:margin files neither a current nor a median operating margin, so the stress margin is set from the worst filed cash-generation year, FY2017, when operating cash flow was 1,055m on revenue of 20,252m (5.2%); 5% sits at or below that trough and below the bear-case 6% margin.
